version: LOCK 46 V1 (9 Nov 2026) - Waraka, the paper mills: the copyist and the fake hadith seller
builds_on: LOCK 34 runner, LOCK 36 (Gate of Knowledge opens after chapter 3). Design references (not shown): Quran 2:282 (let a scribe write with justice); Bukhari 110 (whoever lies about the Prophet deliberately).

waraka.name: Waraka
waraka.text: The river here runs white with pulp. Sheets of paper hang drying between the houses, and every second shop sells ink, pens or books.

waraka.title: The paper-makers' masjid
waraka.text: The walls are lined with shelves of books, and a boy dusts them between prayers.
waraka.first: An old scholar asks what you are reading these days. He seems disappointed by the answer, then kind.

people.name: Yaqub

lines.friendly: “A copyist is a bridge. If the bridge has a hole, everyone after falls through it.”
lines.warm: “Read this back to me. Your eyes are better than mine.”

memory: “The physician sent word: the dose was right. Because you made me copy the page again.”

people.name: Fuad

lines.warm: Fuad has gone quiet these days.

memory: Fuad spits on the ground near your feet.

lines.wary: Zaynab lifts a dripping frame from the vat.
lines.friendly: “Linen rags, beaten for a week. That's what makes it last a thousand years.”
lines.warm: “This sheet is for you. Write something worth keeping on it.”

missions.title: The copyist
missions.button: Yaqub needs someone to read a copy back

a.text: Yaqub has copied a book of medicine for a physician and asks you to read it back against the original. On page forty you find he has skipped a line - a dose. The buyer is waiting outside. “Fixing it means copying the whole page again,” Yaqub says. “Nobody will notice.”

choices.label: Insist he copies the page again

fix.text: Yaqub sighs, sharpens a pen and copies the page again while the buyer waits. When the buyer hears why, he pays extra.

let.text: The buyer takes the book and goes. Yaqub doesn't meet your eye.

fixed: Made Yaqub copy a page again

missions.title: The fake hadith seller
missions.button: Fuad is selling sayings of the Prophet

a.text: Fuad sells strips of paper with sayings “of the Prophet” promising wealth to whoever wears them. One reads: whoever wears this will never be poor. Yaqub says no such saying is in any collection - Fuad wrote it himself.

choices.label: Take Fuad to the scholars of the paper market

scholars.text: The scholars ask Fuad where each saying comes from. He has no answer. They take his strips and burn them in the courtyard, and tell the people why.

warn.text: You tell the people at Fuad's stall what Yaqub told you. Some put their coins back in their purses.

exposed: Exposed the man selling false sayings
